class_guess: Defect-conveyor bouncer with wall phases (1D-CA-like bouncer); no macro law yet
summary: Bouncer over a 0111 field: defects drift left, walls stall growth in irregular phases; no macro law yet
mechanism: The tape is a field of 0111 blocks (runs of three 1s between single 0s) carrying defects: odd runs 1 and 5 (rarely 7, 9) and even runs 0, 2, 4. The head bounces: the left sweep (state E, rule LS) moves every 0 one cell left; the right sweep (F/A, rules RS3 and RSodd) moves it back, so the 0111 field is unchanged by a bounce. Odd defects are transparent: each bounce toggles 11111 <-> 10111 and the defect drifts 2 cells left per bounce (203/203 real defects at 2.86e6). The left end absorbs arriving defects and grows; the right end emits a periodic defect stream (runs 1 3 1 5 5, 20 cells) and grows about 4 cells per 3 bounces.

Even runs are reflectors (rule RSeven: A meets a 0 and turns). Walls of this kind appear at the left end and move right about 3-4 cells per bounce; while one stands, the head never reaches the right part, which freezes, and growth stops. Growth and wall phases alternate irregularly (span 6.4k at 1e8, 129k at 2e10). At 2e10 the tape is a chain of periodic regions in run-length form ((1 3 1 5 5)^3142, (5 1 3 1 5)^2043, a 45-run block ^125, older regions); no law for the phase lengths found.

Halting is possible only as A> 0 0 0 1 (F reading 0000 then 1). The head itself creates four-zero runs inside a sweep (20 times by step 1.3e6), but no 0000 was seen in tape censuses every 1e5 steps to 1e8; no halt to 2e10.

template.note: No proved table within 5 transitions, and no killed machine of ours has this shape (all our templates are counters or Bell eats counter). The closest proof style is upstream's closed-tape-language verifier (CTLv1.v: solve_cert with CPS_LRU / NG / RWL_mod parameters), which fits because halting needs a four-zero run that so far only appears next to the head.

strategy: Two lanes. (a) Certificate lane: a bounded CTL62 parameter sweep (CPS_LRU, NG, RWL_mod) on the three list starts, since halting needs F> 0000 1. (b) Model lane: an exact run-length model (conveyor + RSeven wall motion + left-end absorption + right emitter) to test whether wall phases follow a law or are cryptid-like.
risks: Wall phases start at left-end absorption events whose timing looks irregular; the run-length history may act like a chaotic 1D CA.
Runs of four zeros do occur transiently next to the head, so a regular invariant needs head context.
The three list starts (198, 248, 582) differ only in their history, so a model proof must handle any history.

checkpoint_questions.text: conveyor_2855346: in the rows where the head still reaches the right end (top band), do the thin diagonal stripes all slant left at one angle, none crossing another?
bounces_8e6: below the first rows, are the columns right of the stepped boundary vertical (frozen), while the boundary moves right and several times restarts further left?

No macro law yet: the defect conveyor is exact, but the wall phases look irregular. Should we fund a 2 h stage for a CTL/CPS certificate sweep, or for the exact defect-and-wall model (to decide cryptid or structured), or park?
